plan.title: bug(build-skill): replace missing task test:coverage gate

narratives.Description: content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md requires task test:coverage after every phase, but the Taskfile exposes no test:coverage task and the command exits 200. The skill must alias the task or point at the canonical coverage command already used by task check.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` requires `task test:coverage` after every phase, but the current Taskfile exposes no `test:coverage` task. The command exits 200 and prints the task catalog.

## Reproduction

```text
task test:coverage
```

## Expected

Either provide the documented task alias or update the build skill to invoke the canonical TypeScript coverage command (`pnpm test`) that `task check` already runs.

## Context

Discovered while validating #1692 on current upstream/master after a successful full `task check`.
narratives.UserStory: As an agent following the build skill, I want the documented coverage gate command to exist or be replaced with the canonical coverage command, so that post-phase coverage checks do not exit 200 with a missing task.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Decide between adding a task test:coverage alias that runs the canonical TypeScript coverage command used by task check, or updating content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md (and pack source if projected) to invoke that canonical command.
2. Align any commands.md / Taskfile help text with the chosen spelling.
3. Add a contract test that fails if the build skill references a missing task; CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

narrative.Acceptance: Given the build skill coverage gate, when an agent runs the documented command after a phase, then it invokes a real Taskfile/CLI coverage path and does not exit 200 for a missing task.
Given skill text, Taskfile, and commands reference, when compared, then they use the same coverage command spelling.
Given a content contract test, when the build skill references a coverage task, then the test fails if that task is absent from the Taskfile surface.
